page1.title: Of the Guild
page1.text: The Guild of Lamplighters is older than Hollowmere. We were here before the town, tending the Lightwell, the spring of fire under the hill that feeds the sun. Every lamp in the town is lit from it, and every lamp we light pays a little light back.

page2.title: Of the Hollows
page2.text: A Hollow is a thing that has had its light put out. Beast or man, it does not matter. They are drawn to warmth and they hate it in the same breath. Flame frightens them. A flare in their faces will blind them and burn them twice over.

page3.title: Of the Three Embers
page3.text: When the first Keeper sealed the Lightwell, he split the key into three embers and gave them to three guardians: the Mother of the wood, the Bishop of the tide, and the Choir beneath the hill. While they kept faith, the embers stayed bright.

page4.title: Of Aldric
page4.text: There was a Keeper before me. His name was Aldric. He was the best of us, and he was afraid. A Keeper must one day give his own flame to the Well. Aldric would not. He went down into the dark with his lantern still lit and he did not come back up.

page5.title: Of the Crown
page5.text: I have heard a voice in the well at night. It calls itself a king. It promises that no one need ever give their flame again, that the dark is gentle. It sounds like Aldric. God help me, it sounds like him.

page6.title: Of the Last Lesson
page6.text: If you are reading this, apprentice, then I was too old and too afraid, the same as him. Here is the last lesson. A flame shared is not a flame halved. Two hands on the wick, and neither of you needs to be swallowed. And if you meet him, say his name. Say Aldric. He will remember being a man for one breath, and one breath is enough.
